findings.reason: one extra case (a promoted pointer naming no process and showing no turn in progress is still released) is what makes the "as it is today" clause measurable instead of decorative, and without it the arm set cannot distinguish the intended endpoint from the regression.
findings.text: the deliverable ends "A run that shows no turn in progress is released as it is today, whether or not it names a process", but none of the three release fixtures and none of the four kept cases is a pointer that names no process at all; a worker that implements the leading rule strictly (release only a run whose recorded process is proved dead) passes all seven arms and silently stops releasing the process-less pointers the fleet retires today, because `record_process_alive` answers `None` for a record with no pid (`reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:453-470`)

findings.reason: the plan says which verdict a scheduler-unqueried run gets and says the opposite of the code the node must change, so a worker implementing the sentence would either keep the very fleet population the Why asks it to retire or be refused at the gate for a behaviour the plan never measured.
findings.text: the clause "where such a run names no process, or its scheduler cannot be queried, it stays in progress and is kept" contradicts the release the section measures: `_reviewed_run_is_busy` releases a turn-in-progress run as busy-ended once *either* recorded process is proved dead (`reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:400-402`, `if pointer_alive is False or worker_alive is False: return ""`), and a placed record whose scheduler cannot be queried answers `None` while the run's worker record can still answer `False` (`reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:400-423`), so a placed pointer with an unqueryable scheduler is released today and would be kept under the plan's literal wording

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/crew/pending_*` and `reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py` resolve (`reckon/crew/pending_landing.py` holds `release_merged_promotions`, `recovery_repair_dispatch.py:379` holds `_reviewed_run_is_busy`), the test path is a new file the section declares as a write path, and `s29` carries `data-links=""` so it cites no href to resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the deliverable's closing rule, that a promoted run showing no turn in progress is released whether or not it names a process, has no arm; every arm is a release-or-keep case for a run that names a process, so a strict reading of "proved dead" satisfies the whole done-when while regressing today's release.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the fixture test runs in a temporary crew home, the read-only fleet evaluation lands in the node's manifest under the crew run directory, and the gate is the `all_debug` suite; none of these is a session scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, section number, ticket or version tag reaches a symbol; the population is named by the classification that exists rather than by a new kind, and the write paths and test name the mechanism.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the new clause "where such a run names no process, or its scheduler cannot be queried, it stays in progress and is kept" sets a stricter endpoint than the release this section measures against, and contradicts its own release clause for a placed pointer.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the section carries one verdict, retire the live pointer and worktree of a promoted run whose worker cannot need them, and the measurement population is a skip-condition variant of that same decision rather than a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` carries `s29: [delivered-work-lands-without-a-coordinator#s27]`, `s27` exists and is declared done, and the `informs` key `s29` points at `s10`, which the plan declares `implementable`; the measurement-run classification s29 now relies on is landed code (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:866`, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:3866`), so no upstream is unrecorded.
